candidates.tagline: Ferrari invented a downforce trick 6 teams copied — then Las Vegas happened
candidates.story: Ferrari designed the SF-26 with a unique exhaust wing that uses exhaust gases to generate extra downforce — a system so innovative that six rival teams copied it during 2026. But at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 22, 2026, the design's inherent drag cost both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton over a second per straight; both Ferrari drivers were eliminated in Q2 qualifying, and Max Verstappen pointed to the exhaust wing as the key design weakness at a circuit whose entire identity is going fast in a straight line.
candidates.why_funny: Ferrari built the cleverest aero trick in 2026 F1, got copied by half the grid, then showed up at the one circuit where their brilliant innovation is a liability — and both world-class drivers couldn't even reach the top-10 shootout.
candidates.alt: Lewis Hamilton driving the red Ferrari SF-26 at the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix, the car whose innovative exhaust-wing aero design generates extra downforce but loses straight-line speed on fast circuits like Las Vegas

candidates.tagline: GTA 6's $80 'physical' edition: a game case, an empty disc hub, and nothing else
candidates.story: Grand Theft Auto VI launched November 19, 2026 for $79.99 as the world's biggest-ever game launch; Rockstar confirmed the 'physical' edition contains no game disc — just an empty plastic disc hub and a download code card — and some buyers received boxes with missing or already-redeemed codes; with no disc as a fallback, those buyers paid $80 for a box containing nothing that could install the game. The game comes in at 150GB to download.
candidates.why_funny: The 'physical' in 'physical edition' now means 'you can hold the box' — Rockstar charged $80 for the experience of unboxing a game case to find an empty disc holder and a slip of paper.
candidates.alt: Open GTA VI physical edition case showing an empty plastic disc hub where the game disc would normally sit, with an instruction card pointing to where buyers find the download code
